title: Unknown frame descriptor when loading a Neo4j dump with neo4j-admin load
body:
I create daily dumps in a K8s cluster using `helm` with `neo4j/neo4j` version `5.21.0` and `neo4j-admin database dump` command. Then I wanted to load the dumps into a local volume using `neo4j-admin` version `5.21.2` (same with version `2025.02.0`), which brings up the following error:

```
Caused by: org.neo4j.cli.CommandFailedException: Not a valid Neo4j archive: /backups/neo4j.dump
Caused by: com.github.luben.zstd.ZstdIOException: Unknown frame descriptor
```

Same for running `neo4j-admin database check` on the dump file.

### Actual behavior

The dumps worked fine for several months using the exact same toolchain, but now do not work for a couple of days anymore. So sometimes they work and sometimes not. The dump file size is about 1 GiB and the "uncompressed" size according to `neo4j-admin database load --info` is about 5 GiB. It seems that the `dump` command creates invalid archives or that the `load` command thinks they are invalid.

### Expected behavior

The database dump files can be processed with `neo4j-admin database load` and `neo4j database check` properly.

### Question

Can the dump files be inspected with another tool to check their validity? Since Zstd is used, I tried to extract them with another zstd tooling, but it complains about that it is not a valid archive, even for the dump files checked valid with the `neo4j-admin` tooling.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hi @reporter this looks interesting. It's unclear why the archive seems to be incomplete. We tracked it down to the fact that zstd format expects there to be a padded "frame" of data in the end, which apparently is missing.

The reason why you can't use other zstd tooling to check the file is that neo4j dump process adds a 4 byte header to it. If you want to use some zstd tooling then first get rid of that header by e.g:

`tail -c +5 my-dump-file.dump > my-dump-file.dump.truncated` (yes +5, not +4... tail does some off-by-one weirdness it seems)

And run the tooling on the modified file. You can probably find your dump inside `<neo4j home>/data/dumps/` somewhere.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Thank you for the "wrapping hint", @participant2.

I ran the Zstd tooling to verify whether the problem is on the dump side or on the load side. It seems that the archives in question are already corrupt after dumping:

```
$ tail -c +5 neo4j.dump > neo4j.zstd && zstd -dv neo4j.zstd
*** Zstandard CLI (64-bit) v1.5.5, by Yann Collet ***
neo4j.zstd           : 5.34 GiB...     zstd: neo4j.zstd: unsupported format 
```

The extraction works for the dumps checked valid with `neo4j-admin database load` command. I found out that the extracted file itself is a PAX archive, which then can be extracted using `pax -r < neo4j`. But the problem of creating corrupt dump files persists. The ratio of broken to valid dumps is about 3:1 on our setup.

comments.body:
@reporter  And just to verify (with `hexdump -C --length=10 file` or whatever), the 4 first bytes of the non-modified-by-tailed original dump file should read `DZV1`, does it? (and it's only those bytes that should be pruned away).

And what's your (assuming) Ubuntu version and zstd version in it? Neo4j seems to make native calls to the zstd lib.

There are only two states: Dump works on the first try or will never work regardless how often you try.

I noticed that I was able to restore a backup taken from a Windows host running neo4j version 2025.03.0 in my neo4j instance on Kube running version 2025.05.1, but I wasn't able to take a backup on Kube and restore the same backup on the same instance.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
I can't seem to reproduce this issue which makes it really hard to narrow down. We use Apache Commons Compress to create the tarball, which we in turn compress using ZSTD (java bindings from luben).

From the looks of the stacktraces provided and the implementation of commons compress it can just as well be a broken tarball, forcing ZSTD to read past the archive. It seems to be triggered by the "shape" of the data. The Neo4j code for dump mostly just delegates to these libraries, so the bug likely hides outside neo4j. But if can understand when it happens we can possibly work around it.

To find and fix this issue we probably need a reliable reproducer, or at least a broken dump file to inspect, to try and find out exactly how the data corruption looks like. If anyone can provide these we would much appreciate it!

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
It appears that the bug is in `--overwrite-destination`. When an existing larger archive exists it was not overwritten properly, leaving some old data at the tail of the new archive, which caused ZSTD to crash. A fix will be included in the next patch release of 5.LTS and in the next 2025.X release. A work around for other affected versions is to not use the `--overwrite-destination` but manually (or scripted) remove the previous dump prior to creating the new one.

Thank you for reporting this issue!
